303881e4db (the parent of the first PHY commit, i.e. feature source absent

RESOLVED on hardware 2026-08-24 with three boards.

=== ESP32-C3: CONFIRMED supports 2M and Coded ===
ble.config('phys') == 7 (0b111). Genuine controller read via NimBLE's cached
LE features (a failed read would return 1, not 7).

=== CYW43439 (Pico W / Pico 2 W): CONFIRMED supports NEITHER ===
With a capable ESP32-C3 as central, asking the Pico 2 W to change PHY:
  gap_set_phy(h, tx_phy=PHY_2M)    -> OSError -538
  gap_set_phy(h, tx_phy=PHY_CODED) -> OSError -538
-538 = BLE_HS_ERR_HCI_BASE(0x200) + 0x1A = BLE_ERR_UNSUPP_REM_FEATURE,
"Unsupported Remote Feature" -- the REMOTE end refusing on air.
Corroborated by the 43439 BT firmware blob identifying as CYW4343A2, a
Bluetooth 4.2 era LE core. "Bluetooth 5.2" on the datasheet describes the
module, not LE PHY support.

=== POSITIVE CONTROL: C3 <-> C3 both PHY changes SUCCEED ===
  2M    request=ok events=[(1, 2, 2)]
  CODED request=ok events=[(1, 4, 4)]
_IRQ_PHY_UPDATE fired with (conn_handle, tx_phy, rx_phy) and the correct
bitmask values (PHY_2M=0x02, PHY_CODED=0x04). This also proves
nimble_phy_to_mask() converts correctly: NimBLE reports Coded as enum 3 and
the API correctly yields mask 4.

This validates the entire NimBLE implementation end to end on real hardware:
capability query, gap_set_phy(), the IRQ event, and the enum/mask conversion.

DOCS IMPLICATION: rp2 / Pico W / Pico 2 W cannot use 2M or Coded at all, so
PR 1 is of no benefit there and the docs should say so. ESP32-C3 is the
natural first board to enable it on.

Skips via multitest.skip() when:
 - the firmware lacks gap_set_phy (feature compiled out),
 - config("phys") says the controller has no 2M support,
 - a backend that can't report capability has the request refused.

Hardware verified:
 - ESP32-C3 + ESP32-S3 with the feature enabled -> pass
 - ESP32-C3 + stock ESP32-C3 (no feature)       -> skip

Notes for anyone extending this:
 - multitest.skip() only works INSIDE instanceN(); the multitest class is
   appended after the test body by run-multitests.py.
 - Don't reference bluetooth.PHY_2M before the hasattr guard, or old firmware
   raises AttributeError before the skip can fire.
 - Only 2M is covered. Coded PHY needs the same treatment but the PHY value
   reported back is 4 (S2 and S8 are indistinguishable at this layer).

Resolved: no sdkconfig work is needed for PR 1.

Checked ESP-IDF v5.5.2, components/bt/host/nimble/Kconfig.in:

  menuconfig BT_NIMBLE_50_FEATURE_SUPPORT
      depends on BT_NIMBLE_ENABLED && (SOC_BLE_50_SUPPORTED || !BT_CONTROLLER_ENABLED)
      default y
      config BT_NIMBLE_LL_CFG_FEAT_LE_2M_PHY     default y
      config BT_NIMBLE_LL_CFG_FEAT_LE_CODED_PHY  default y

So on any SOC_BLE_50_SUPPORTED target (C3, S3, C2, C6, H2) both PHYs are
already on by default. The original ESP32 lacks SOC_BLE_50_SUPPORTED, so they
are off -- which matches the hardware capability table (ESP32 original: no 2M,
no Coded).

Also confirmed ble_gap_set_prefered_le_phy() and
ble_gap_set_prefered_default_le_phy() in ble_gap.c are gated only on
NIMBLE_BLE_CONNECT, not on the PHY Kconfig symbols, so they always link.

This is consistent with the hardware result: enabling only
MICROPY_PY_BLUETOOTH_ENABLE_PHY_SELECTION in mpconfigboard.h was sufficient to
get working 2M and Coded PHY switching on ESP32-C3 and ESP32-S3, with no
sdkconfig edits.

Conclusion: the original premise (that ESP32 needs separate sdkconfig plumbing
because extmod/nimble/syscfg/syscfg.h does not apply) is true in principle but
moot in practice -- IDF's defaults already match what PR 1 needs.
